# Testing and acceptance

CTest registers eleven release-candidate tests:

1. deterministic unit/audio/model/error/metrics/hash checks;
2. ASR/VAD/TTS streaming, continuity, partial/final and terminal ownership;
3. 10,000 repeated model/session lifecycle cycles;
4. same-session `BUSY` plus eight-session concurrency;
5. 100 idempotent cancellation cycles and barge-in cancellation;
6. malformed RIFF corpus and invalid ABI/audio inputs;
7. 5,000 tiny streaming chunks/backpressure stress;
8. 5,000 random WAV blobs + 1,000 random PCM pipelines;
9. C99 compile/layout/runtime ABI smoke;
10. all CLI commands, expected outputs, malformed failure, JSON/CSV benchmarks;
11. compiled descriptor/registry/model-license metadata consistency.

Fixtures are synthetic and regenerated by `tests/generate_fixtures.py`; `scripts/verify_fixtures.sh` proves SHA reproducibility. Optional `IBAUDIO_BUILD_LIBFUZZER=ON` builds a libFuzzer entrypoint when the compiler supplies that runtime.

Run:

```sh
ctest --test-dir build/linux-release --output-on-failure
python3 scripts/check_abi.py build/linux-release/libibaudio.so abi/ibaudio_symbols_v1.txt
```

ASan+UBSan with leak detection passed 11/11 locally via `scripts/run_sanitizers.sh`; exact output is under `reports/`. ThreadSanitizer is a separate future lane; concurrency behavior is still functionally stress-tested.
